chunks: Verily God knows the unknown of the heavens and the earth; and God perceives all you do.

key_terms.غَيْبَ: The unseen or hidden realm known only to God

ai.seo_question: What does the Quran say about God's knowledge of the unseen and human actions?
ai.summary: This verse, frequently cited in Shia tafsir as a cornerstone of divine omniscience, underscores that God's knowledge of the unseen (ghayb) is absolute and encompasses both the celestial and terrestrial realms. It reinforces the concept of 'Basir' (All-Seeing), reminding believers that every hidden and apparent action is witnessed by the Divine, a theme central to the doctrine of 'Ilm al-Ghayb' in Imami theology. The verse serves as a spiritual anchor for self-accountability (muhasabah), encouraging believers to maintain consciousness of God's presence in all aspects of life.
